title: The Meal Offering
iast: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahmakarmasamādhinā ||
en: the offering is brahman / the oblation is brahman / poured by brahman into the fire of brahman / brahman alone is reached / by one absorbed in the action that is brahman
brief: Offering-instrument, oblation, sacrificial fire, offerer and goal are all said to be Brahman. Lakshmanjoo reads this through Śiva.
logic: Eating becomes an occasion to notice giver, gift and recipient in one field of awareness.
howto: When: Before the first bite. Practice: Set down utensils. If following the taught custom, place a little clean water in the palm, recite the full verse, then eat. The short line is an optional memory cue, not a replacement prescribed by the Gītā. Return: Eat normally, gratefully and attentively.
how: Before the first bite: put a little water in the palm, look at the food, and say the verse once. Then eat as if the meal is being offered into a fire — slowly, without hurry. The feeling to find: gratitude with heat. Nothing extra; the verse does the whole work.
sign: Everyday integration: Eat normally, gratefully and attentively.

title: Śiva Bows to Śiva
iast: asmadrūpa samāviṣṭaḥ svātmanātma nivāraṇe | śivaḥ karotu nijayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane ||
en: śiva, having entered the form that is myself, bows — by his own power — to śiva, for the removal of the obstacle that is himself.
brief: The author asks Śiva, present as one’s own form and veiling himself through his own nature, to make an offering of homage to himself through his own power.
logic: The actor, the impediment and the addressed Lord are contemplated within Śiva’s self-relation.
howto: When: Before a meal, particularly if it follows Brahmārpaṇam. Practice: Read or say the complete verse. Do not turn it into a ritual to erase guilt on command. Return: Eat or return to the person sharing the meal.
how: Say it silently as the food arrives. The 'obstacle' can be anything — the craving, the guilt, the person you're eating with. Name it, then let the verse dissolve it.
feel: the moment of placing should feel like relief, like putting something down.
sign: Everyday integration: Eat or return to the person sharing the meal.

title: The Sense-Goddesses Offer Bhairava
iast: ātmīyaviṣayabhogairindriyadevyaḥ sadā hṛdambhoje | abhipūjayanti yaṃ taṃ cinmayamānandabhairavaṃ vande
en: with feasts of their own sense-objects, the sense-goddesses ever worship, in the heart-lotus, him — the consciousness-made bliss-bhairava: i praise.
brief: The sense-goddesses constantly worship consciousness-filled Ānandabhairava with their enjoyment of their own objects, in the lotus of the heart.
logic: A sense-experience can be understood as offering rather than as something outside spiritual practice.
howto: When: At the first taste of food. Practice: Take one ordinary bite. Notice taste as taste, then recite the closing praise if desired. Return: Enjoy the meal without needing to intensify sensations.
how: At the first bite, feel the heart-lotus (just behind the centre of the chest) as the altar and the flavour as the flower landing on it. Three bites only — overdoing it kills the taste. The feeling: gratitude with heat. The sense is honoured as a goddess, not supervised as a thief.
sign: Everyday integration: Enjoy the meal without needing to intensify sensations.

title: Homage to the World-Formed
iast: prapañcottīrṇarūpāya namaste viśvamūrtaye | sadādivyaprakāśāya svātmane'nantaśaktaye
en: homage to the form that has crossed beyond the manifest — to the self of the world's form; to the ever-divinely-shining, to the self that is unending power.
brief: Homage to the One whose form is the universe, yet who is beyond its manifest forms.
logic: The room need not become extraordinary; it is included in what is addressed.
howto: When: On first opening the eyes, before touching the phone. Practice: Look once at whatever is actually there—ceiling, light, window. Recite the short invocation once, or the complete verse if learned. Return: Get up and attend to the day.
how: On waking: recite as its placement asks. The verse's own act is namaḥ — homage, phrase by phrase, one round.
sign: Everyday integration: Get up and attend to the day.
what: The maṅgala names its object twice: the world's form — crossed beyond, yet still his; and the ever-divine-shining self whose power does not end. Homage lands on what already shines, not on something far away.

title: The Body-Temple Offering
iast: deho devālayaḥ proktaḥ svātmā devaḥ sanātanaḥ | tyajedajñānanirmālyaṃ so'haṃ bhāvena pūjayet
en: the body is declared god's temple, the own self the eternal god. casting off the sweepings of ignorance, let him worship with the feeling: i-am-he.
brief: The body is called the deity’s temple, and one’s Self the enduring deity. This is a traditional maxim; its attribution as verse 1 of Abhinavagupta’s Dehasthadevatācakra is not supported by the checked witness.
logic: Respect the body as a place of worship, including when tired, ordinary or uncomfortable.
howto: When: While still in bed or just sitting up. Practice: Be aware of the whole body, without requiring it to feel calm or sacred. Say the half-verse slowly. Return: Stand, wash, and care for it.
how: The verse's own method: cast off the sweepings of ignorance and hold so'ham as the worship — the bhāva is the practice, not a formula.
sign: Everyday integration: Stand, wash, and care for it.
what: The frame vow: the body is proclaimed god's temple and the own self the eternal god; the sweepings of ignorance are cast off, and worship happens as I-am-He feeling.

title: The Three States as His Rays
iast: jāgratasvapnasuṣuptyādyā dhārayaṃśca nijāḥ kalāḥ | svecchayā bhāsi naṭavan niṣkalo'si ca tattvataḥ
en: waking, dreaming, deep sleep and the rest — you hold them as your own portions. By your will you shine like an actor, yet you are partless in truth.
brief: Waking, dreaming, and deep sleep are described as expressions of the Lord, who is nevertheless partless in reality.
logic: Recognise a change of state without needing to locate an additional permanent mental object.
howto: When: At the transition out of sleep. Practice: Name the state you have just left, then say the short clause “yet in truth you are without parts.” Return: Begin ordinary morning activity.
how: On waking: say it once. The verse itself performs the recognition — the states named as his rays, nothing else to do.
sign: Everyday integration: Begin ordinary morning activity.
what: Waking, dreaming, deep sleep and the rest are held as his own rays: he shines by his own will like an actor, and is partless in truth. The states borrow the light; he does not play the parts.

title: From Your Waking, His Waking
iast: tvatprabodhāt prabodho'sya tvannidrāto layo'sya yat | atastvadātmakaṃ sarvaṃ viśva sadasadātmakam
en: from your waking comes his waking; from your sleep comes his merging. hence all is of your nature — the world, both real and unreal.
brief: The verse relates waking and dissolution to the Lord, and concludes that the entire world is of that nature.
logic: The day can be released without demanding to control the night.
howto: When: Just before sleep. Practice: Recall the short conclusion once. No breath manipulation or effort to remain aware through sleep is required. Return: Turn off the light and sleep.
how: Last line of the day. Lie down and take one awake minute: you are about to do what he does at night. Don't stay awake doing this — fall asleep inside the thought.
feel: as the eyes close, feel the day's edges get soft, 'unreal' — that softening is sadasadātmakam. If anxious at night, this dissolves the day rather than reviewing it.
sign: Everyday integration: Turn off the light and sleep.

title: In Sleep, When the Outer Range Perished
iast: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare | sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate
en: in the not-yet-come sleep, when the outer range has perished — that state, to be gone to by mind, the supreme goddess shines forth.
brief: When sleep is approaching and outward objects fade, the verse presents that transitional condition as a place where the supreme Goddess shines.
logic: The movement toward sleep can be included in awareness.
howto: When: As drowsiness naturally comes. Practice: Read the verse earlier if necessary; at bedtime simply notice the transition without fighting to keep it. Return: Allow sleep to arrive.
how: At lights-out, on your back, one hand on the belly. Wait for the outer field to fade — sounds go dull, images slow. Then instead of following sleep passively, send the mind as an arrow to the heart-centre, once. Then release. The Goddess-feel is a hum or warmth behind the chest; if images swarm you have grasped — release and let the hum carry. Single-shot: no repetitions.
sign: Everyday integration: Allow sleep to arrive.

title: At Your Cool Feet
en: when will i lie down — free of every object, settled in the embrace of undiminished glory — at your two cool lotus feet?
brief: Utpaladeva longs to rest at the cool lotus feet of the Lord within a condition of fullness and intimacy.
logic: Devotional rest can be imagined without treating the image as a literal bodily event.
howto: When: When lying down to sleep. Practice: Read the full verse slowly; allow the imagery of cooling and rest to remain poetic. Return: Let attention turn away from the day.
how: In bed. Say it once, then let the image of the two cool feet form under the mind's eye — no details needed, just the coolness. The feeling to find: the fever of the day dropping. If the mind races, return to the coolness, not the words.
sign: Everyday integration: Let attention turn away from the day.

title: I Don't Mind
en: in crisis or at ease, weeping or laughing, grave or unhinged — by devotion, lord, let me be so.
brief: The speaker asks to remain in devotion whether troubled or at ease, weeping or laughing, solemn or unsettled.
logic: Devotion need not depend on securing a pleasant state.
howto: When: During travel, waiting or an unplanned interruption. Practice: Recite the whole verse in four short quarters if learned; first practise just the paired conditions. Return: Continue the wait without pretending to enjoy it.
how: Use it when waiting has turned into agitation — a queue, a delay, a message that won't come. Say it once inwardly. Don't wait for composure: the very mess is the place where devotion can be.
feel: the shoulders drop half a millimetre; that's the api doing its work.
sign: Everyday integration: Continue the wait without pretending to enjoy it.

title: In Every Action
en: o lord, may i experience, moment by moment, in every action, the great joy of drinking the nectar of your worship.
brief: The speaker longs to taste the joy of worship in every act, moment after moment.
logic: A transition can be remembered as worship without needing to produce ecstasy.
howto: When: Between ordinary activities. Practice: Say the small temporal phrase, or the entire prayer when it is memorised. Pause for one ordinary breath. Return: Move to the next action.
how: At any transition or pause: say it once, then take one breath as if that breath were the nectar. Don't manufacture joy — notice the small lift that a pause already gives. Three pauses, three sips, and the waiting has changed colour.
sign: Everyday integration: Move to the next action.

title: No Fear-Talk
iast: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti | satsv api durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu
en: with you as lord, all-pervading in own self — therefore no talk of transmigration-fear. even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts are present.
brief: When the Lord is recognised as the all-pervading Self, fear of repeated worldly existence is denied, even while difficult karma and suffering may remain.
logic: The verse speaks to a metaphysical fear; it does not deny bodily pain or replace treatment.
howto: When: When unwell or frightened by what might happen. Practice: Recite the short reassurance, or the full verse if it is familiar. Name the specific practical need separately. Return: Rest, seek care, or ask someone for help as needed.
how: When negative, say it and let the concession stand: yes, this is hard; and the fear of it is separate from the pain itself. The verse splits them.
feel: the pain stays, the story about the pain thins. That thinning is the verse working.
sign: Everyday integration: Rest, seek care, or ask someone for help as needed.

title: Yoke the Mind
iast: evameva parā pūjā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā | aikyabuddhayā tu sarveśe mano deve niyojayet
en: just so is the highest worship — in every state, at all times: with a mind of oneness, one should yoke the mind to god as the lord of all.
brief: The verse calls for an understanding of unity, directing the mind toward the Lord across all conditions.
logic: Offering is not abandoning the task; careful work can embody devotion.
howto: When: Before opening a work task. Practice: Say the opening clause once: “Just so is the highest worship.” Choose the next concrete action. Return: Start the task and complete one small unit.
how: Before opening the laptop: one line, then begin. The test for aikyabuddhi: the boundary of your skin thins. If it sharpens, you're thinking oneness, not yoking it — drop to the breath and restart. Each task is one yoke; re-hitch as often as needed.
sign: Everyday integration: Start the task and complete one small unit.

title: Achieve God in Activity
en: so the devotee is told: become śiva and worship. you yourself are the essence of the body, purified by devotion's non-duality.
brief: The verse invokes the teaching to worship Śiva having become Śiva, and examines devotion through nonduality.
logic: The one who worships and the worshipped are contemplated as nonseparate.
howto: When: When work seems incompatible with practice. Practice: Say the short injunction once before beginning. No need to pretend the work has changed substance. Return: Perform the ordinary task responsibly.
how: At the desk, when work feels like a distraction from practice: say it and reclassify. The spreadsheet, the email, the conversation — that is the worship.
feel: the task itself becomes slightly luminous; do it as offering, not as interruption.
sign: Everyday integration: Perform the ordinary task responsibly.

title: I-Making Flowers
iast: kurute bhairavapūjāmanaladalasthā'bhimānakusumairyā | nityamahaṅkṛtirūpāṃ vande tāṃ śāmbhavīmambām
en: who performs bhairava's worship, standing in fire's petal, with flowers of i-making — ever of i-making form, i praise her, the mother śāmbhavī.
brief: The hymn represents ahaṃkṛti, I-making, as a goddess whose flowers of self-assertion worship Bhairava.
logic: Even this mental movement is something to recognise and work with, not necessarily eradicate by force.
howto: When: When pride, embarrassment or wanting credit becomes very conspicuous. Practice: Acknowledge that impulse without dramatizing it. Recite the praise of Śāmbhavī if learned. Return: Credit others fairly and continue.
how: When the ego flares mid-task — pride, irritation at the colleague, hunger for recognition: see it as a flower, pick it, place it at the heart's fire. Three flowers are enough.
feel: relief, like putting down a bag; the fire (warmth at the solar plexus) confirms it.
sign: Everyday integration: Credit others fairly and continue.

title: When Your Form Expands
iast: tvatsvarūpe jṛmbhamāṇe tvaṃ cāhaṃ cākhilaṃ jagat | jāte tasya tirodhāne na tvaṃ nāhaṃ na vai jagat
en: when your own form expands — you and i and the whole world. when its withdrawal is born — neither you, nor i, nor indeed the world.
brief: As the Lord’s own form expands, you, I, and the entire world appear; when it withdraws, these distinctions no longer appear.
logic: Experience need not be carried as though its totality were the private burden of one small self.
howto: When: When work becomes overwhelming. Practice: Say the short catalogue of “you, I, the whole world,” then name the next necessary task. Return: Do one thing at a time.
how: Use it at the overwhelm point — too much to do, the self tightening. Say it and feel the day as one exhale of a larger form. The overwhelm thins because the 'me' carrying it is part of the expansion, not its owner. Then return to the next small task.
sign: Everyday integration: Do one thing at a time.

title: The Speech-Goddess
iast: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ viṣayakusumakḷptārcaḥ | prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya
en: having made the speech-goddess one's own light, with sense-flowers arranged as offering — bowing to the guru, first unfolding, then entering the heart.
brief: The poet describes speech as a Goddess and sense-objects as flowers of worship, followed by bowing and entering the heart.
logic: Treat words as something offered, and therefore worthy of care.
howto: When: Before a difficult conversation. Practice: Pause for one natural breath and read or recall the verse. Listen to the other person before deciding what to say. Return: Speak plainly rather than trying to sound mystical.
how: Before a difficult conversation, a speech, a message you'll regret: one breath, hand on the throat. Make the speech a light — not a blade. Offering the sense-flowers means: don't weaponise what you've seen and heard. Then speak from the heart-entered place, not the throat.
sign: Everyday integration: Speak plainly rather than trying to sound mystical.

title: Every Sound Is Mantra
iast: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
en: whatever sound arises from the mouth — that mantra is transcendent. whatever posture of the pleasure-pain-born body — that indeed is mudrā. whatever flowing of breath by its own rhythm — that indeed is wonderful yoga. the supreme śākta abode — while i experience, what indeed would not shine?
brief: The verse presents ordinary sound, bodily posture and breath in an expansive register: mantra, mudrā and yoga, when recognised in consciousness.
logic: Notice that ordinary speaking is part of experience rather than outside spiritual life.
howto: When: After saying something ordinary, not just before a formal chant. Practice: Recall the phrase once. Avoid turning it into permission for careless speech. Return: Return attention to the person present.
how: Use it after you've said something — ordinary, even stupid. That was mantra. The recognition flips the whole day: the meeting, the small talk, the complaint — all of it is mantra, mudrā, yoga, shining.
feel: the mouth becomes a temple; be careful what you put on the altar.
sign: Everyday integration: Return attention to the person present.

title: Enough of Difference-Talk
iast: alaṃ bhedānukathayā tvadbhaktirasacarvaṇāt | sarvamekamidaṃ śāntamiti vaktuṃ ca lajjate
en: enough of difference-talk — chewing the sap of devotion to you: all this is one, at peace; and even to say so feels shy.
brief: Enough of repeated discourse on distinctions. In the whole verse, the savour of devotion renders even the declaration “all is one” inadequate.
logic: Nonduality is not another argument that must be won.
howto: When: When a discussion becomes performative, especially a spiritual argument. Practice: Say the short phrase inwardly once. Listen and consider whether another explanation is useful. Return: Respond accurately if needed—or let the point rest.
how: Use it when an argument about views has you mid-sentence — or when you're about to explain your practice to someone who doesn't need it. Stop. The shyness is the right register.
feel: looking away slightly, a small heat in the face — let the body do the disarming.
sign: Everyday integration: Respond accurately if needed—or let the point rest.

title: What Bath for the Stainless?
iast: nirmalasya kutaḥ snānaṃ vastraṃ viśvodarasya ca | nirlepasya kuto gandho ramyasyābharaṇaṃ kutaḥ
en: for the stainless, what bath? for the world-bellied, what garment? for the unanointed, what scent? for the lovely, what jewel?
brief: The Lord is already stainless. Why would a bath purify the one who is beyond impurity?
logic: The water cares for a body, while the verse challenges the idea that the absolute needs cleaning.
howto: When: While washing hands or showering. Practice: Ask the rhetorical question once and wash normally. Return: Dry yourself and leave.
how: In the shower: name each item as you use it — water for the stainless, towel for the world-bellied, scent for the unanointed. The mismatch is the smile.
feel: the water becomes an offering rather than a chore; three items, three small bows.
sign: Everyday integration: Dry yourself and leave.

title: This Body for Worship
en: may this body of mine — nourished by the clear, bright nectar of devotion rising within — be fit only for your worship.
brief: May this body, nourished by devotion, become suitable for worship of You.
logic: Devotion can be embodied as how the body is used in the next activity.
howto: When: After bathing or getting dressed. Practice: Say the final petition while placing your hands at rest; no imposed gesture or pose. Return: Go do one useful thing.
how: Dressed, before leaving the bathroom: say it once and feel the freshly washed body as anointed rather than merely clean. The day ahead is the pūjā; the body is the instrument.
feel: a slight uprightness in the spine — the instrument picking itself up.
sign: Everyday integration: Go do one useful thing.

title: The Play of the Dawning
iast: udayāvabhāsacarvaṇalīlāṃ viśvasya yā karotyaniśam | ānandabhairavīṃ tāṃ vimarśarūpāmahaṃ vande
en: the play of the dawning, shining forth, and chewing over of the universe, which she performs unceasingly — bliss-bhairavī, her, whose form is reflection, i praise.
brief: The hymn praises Ānandabhairavī, whose reflective awareness is linked with the world’s appearing, shining, and being relished.
logic: What appears and the knowing of it can be contemplated together.
howto: When: At dawn or the first visible change in daylight. Practice: Notice light arriving and recite the closing praise of the Goddess. No visualisation is necessary. Return: Open the curtains or leave the room.
how: At dawn, as placed: the verse's own act is vande — praise of the ceaseless play she keeps performing.
sign: Everyday integration: Open the curtains or leave the room.
what: Ānanda-Bhairavī as vimarśa — the awareness-energy that chews the universe ceaselessly, non-different from Śiva as heat from fire: one aggregate of awareness, her reflection-form.

title: Waving-Lights for the Self-Shining
iast: svayaṃ prakāśamānasya kuto nīrājanaṃ vibhoḥ | vedavācāmavedyasya kutaḥ stotraṃ vidhīyate
en: whence waving-lights for the self-shining lord? how is a hymn enjoined for him whom the veda cannot say?
brief: What use is waving a lamp before the Lord who shines by himself? The verse questions the adequacy of outward ritual.
logic: The gesture may train attention, rather than supply something missing to Śiva.
howto: When: At the mirror, or when turning on a light. Practice: Say the question once. If using a lamp, do so safely; an imagined offering is optional. Return: Finish your washing or dressing.
how: At the bathroom mirror, hand raised with the light: you are the lamp-bearer, and the face that brightens is the audience. Hum, don't articulate — you have just honoured the Vedavācāmavedya.
feel: the chest brightens before the mirror does.
sign: Everyday integration: Finish your washing or dressing.

title: Pardon for the Unseen
iast: pūrṇasya dakṣiṇā kutra nityatṛptasya tarpaṇam | visarjanaṃ vyāpakasyā'pratyakṣasya kṣamāpaṇam
en: where is the fee for the full? libation for the ever-content? dismissal for the all-pervading? pardon for the unseen?
brief: The litany asks what gift, libation, dismissal or request for pardon could be offered to the complete, ever-content, all-pervading Lord.
logic: A closing bow is not a transaction with a distant deity.
howto: When: When ending a small devotional act. Practice: Read the complete verse slowly. Let its questions complete the ritual without adding another elaborate ending. Return: Put the towel or ritual item away.
how: Use it at the end of the bath as the day's closing already: one bow, weight the last word — pardon. The feeling is the end of accounting: no tally of errors, no debt. Guilt arrives, is named as one of the litany's items, and dissolves with the god it expected to offend.
sign: Everyday integration: Put the towel or ritual item away.

title: When Your Words Are Not Heard
iast: brūṣe nottamāṅga paśyasi na māmetādṛśaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vijñaptiṃ bahudhā kṛtāṃ na śṛṇuṣe nāyāsi manmānase | saṃsārārṇavagartamadhyapatitaṃ prāyeṇa nālambase vākcakṣuḥśravaṇāṅghriṇādirahitaṃ tvāmāha satyaṃ śrutiḥ
en: you speak not, o best-limbed one; you look not upon me, wretched as i am. my entreaty, made in many ways, you hear not; you come not into my mind. fallen amid the pit of the ocean of transmigration, i am mostly left unsupported — yet scripture truly declares you devoid of speech, sight, hearing, feet and the like!
brief: The devotee complains that the Lord does not speak, look, listen or intervene—then recalls the scriptural denial of such bodily faculties.
logic: Devotional address may include protest without pretending that silence has ceased.
howto: When: When prayer feels unanswered. Practice: Read the complaint as a lament; do not force a cheerful reversal. Return: Make whatever real-world request for help is needed.
how: Use it when you've spoken and nobody heard — human or divine. Say the whole complaint with feeling; the scripture-clause at the end is the punchline that dissolves it.
feel: the irritation turns to laughter mid-verse; that laugh is the prasāda.
sign: Everyday integration: Make whatever real-world request for help is needed.

title: Devouring Māyā as Food
en: o nātha, your devotees roam happy on the shore of the world, filled and satisfied by consuming māyā, time, fate and desire themselves.
brief: The devotees are depicted as satisfied by consuming the very structures of limiting experience—māyā, time, necessity, attachment and the like.
logic: What ordinarily binds can become material for recognition.
howto: When: When desire or dissatisfaction accompanies a meal. Practice: Read the verse as a poetic vision; avoid turning ordinary eating into a literal ritual of consuming metaphysical categories. Return: Eat with care and attend to what is actually needed.
how: Before or after a meal, when desire is loudest: name it as the course — māyā, time, fate, desire — and eat it. The hunger is the menu.
feel: the wanting transforms into satedness mid-sentence; that flip is the verse working.
sign: Everyday integration: Eat with care and attend to what is actually needed.

title: Abandon Nothing, Grasp Nothing
iast: saṃsāro 'sti na tattvatas tanubhṛtāṃ bandhasya vārtaiva kā bandho yasya na jātu tasya vitathā muktasya muktikriyā | mithyāmohakṛd eṣa rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramo mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svastho yathāvasthitaḥ
en: saṃsāra is not, in truth, for body-holders — of bondage, what news? bondage never truly is for anyone — so for the free, liberation-rite is false. this error-maker is rope-snake-shadow-ghost-delusion. abandon nothing; grasp nothing; live healthy, staying as you are.
brief: The verse challenges the assumed reality of bondage, ending with an invitation to stop grasping and rejecting.
logic: Let experience appear without the immediate demand to keep or eliminate it.
howto: When: In a queue, during uncertainty, or when scrolling compulsively. Practice: Say the two prohibitions once. Unclench a hand only if it helps; no ritual hand movement is required. Return: Choose the next sensible action.
how: In the queue, the delay, the silence: say the last line — 'live healthy, staying as you are.' The restlessness wants to grab something or drop something; the verse forbids both.
feel: the hands open and close once, then rest; the waiting is now the living.
sign: Everyday integration: Choose the next sensible action.

title: Two Classes of People
en: there are two classes found in this universe: one class is of ordinary people, and another are those who are thy devotees.
brief: The hymn opens an inquiry into concealment: what hides Śiva for ordinary consciousness and what does not hide him for the devotee?
logic: Distinguish the apparent obscuring condition from the object itself.
howto: When: When caught in a habitual interpretation that blocks a fresh look. Practice: Do not publish a recitation until the complete Sanskrit has been collated. For now use the English question as a study reflection. Return: Look again at the actual situation.
how: Use it in any crowd — the queue, the train, the meeting. Run the census once: two classes. Then check which one is noticing the census.
feel: a small private smile; nobody can tell from the outside which class you're in — that's the point.
sign: Everyday integration: Look again at the actual situation.

title: Bliss Is the Forgotten Treasure
iast: ānando 'tra na vittamadhyamadavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛtaprabhāprakaravan naiva prakāśodayaḥ | harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ
en: bliss here is not wealth-middle-intoxication, nor like enjoying women, nor lamp-sun-moon-made splendour-multitude — and not the light-rise either. joy with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground, like burden-lowering, is the attainment of the forgotten treasure of the all-nonduality state — the light-rise.
brief: The verse distinguishes the joy of nondual recognition from possession, intoxication and sensory splendour, likening recognition to recovering a forgotten treasure and lowering a burden.
logic: A teaching about intrinsic fullness can be contemplated alongside the fatigue that is actually present.
howto: When: When looking back over an exhausting day. Practice: Read the passage as a comparison. Do not demand bliss before being permitted to sleep. Return: Rest.
how: In bed, say it and feel the day's weight as the literal bhāra being lowered. Bliss here is not an event but an unloading.
feel: the shoulders drop a centimetre deeper each line; by the last line the bed has the treasure under it.
sign: Everyday integration: Rest.

title: Forgetting, and the Final Plea
iast: yātastvatsahavāsato bahutaraḥ kālo vatāsmin kṣaṇe kiṃ kiṃ vā na kṛtaṃ tvayā varagurūpāsānimittena me | vāraṃ vāramahaṃ punarnirupamāṃ divyaṃ bhuvaṃ prāsuvatkāyastvāṃ kila vismarāmi yadataḥ stheyaṃ na bhūyastvayā
en: much time dwelling with you has passed — alas, in this very moment! what, what has not been done by you for me, for the sake of serving the excellent guru! again and again i, whose body has attained the incomparable divine plane — yet indeed i forget you. therefore, by you let there be no further staying-away!
brief: The speaker acknowledges that, even after divine assistance, he keeps forgetting the Lord. The prayer becomes a candid plea rather than a display of attainment.
logic: Forgetting need not prevent another act of devotion.
howto: When: When exhausted, ill or spiritually discouraged. Practice: Read as much of the complete verse as is accessible. The short phrase “I indeed forget you” can be remembered as a confession, not as a separately transmitted mantra. Return: Take medicine, rest or reconnect with someone if needed.
how: When ill and feeling forgotten: say the whole verse as the complaint it is — 'what has not been done by you for me?' — and let the last line be the request.
feel: the forgetting is admitted first (you forgot him); the plea is fair because of that. One round, then rest.
sign: Everyday integration: Take medicine, rest or reconnect with someone if needed.

title: Dance with the Foot-Dust
en: when will that glorious day come to me, my lord — your lotus-foot dust anointing my hair — that i may dance the dance begun from the endless?
brief: Utpaladeva asks when the dust of the Lord’s lotus feet will adorn him and he will dance in overflowing joy.
logic: Longing itself is part of devotion; inability to dance is not a failure.
howto: When: When bodily limitations make joy feel far away. Practice: Read it as an open question rather than a demand for immediate transformation. Return: Make room for whatever care the body needs.
how: From the sickbed, say it as a question — kadā, when — without demanding the answer today. Picture only the dust on the hair; the dance can wait.
feel: longing itself becomes the posture; the verse sanctifies not-yet.
sign: Everyday integration: Make room for whatever care the body needs.

title: Whatever Is Seen Is You
iast: antardehe mayā nityaṃ tvamātmā ca gaveṣitaḥ | na dṛṣṭastvaṃ nacaivātmā yacca dṛṣṭaṃ tvameva tat
en: inside the body, sought by me always — you as self, and the self is never seen. whatever is seen is you alone, that.
brief: The seeker looks inward for the Self and does not find it as an object; what is seen is nevertheless affirmed as the Lord’s appearance.
logic: The contemplative claim is about recognition, not proof that pain is imaginary.
howto: When: When the body or circumstances feel alien. Practice: Look at one ordinary thing and recite the final clause if learned. Return: Attend to the condition or task directly.
how: When pain or weakness is present: look at it once — the ache as an object — and name it 'seen: you.' Not as denial of pain but as address change.
feel: the pain stays but loses its claim to be yours; it's his visible side, and visibility is already grace.
sign: Everyday integration: Attend to the condition or task directly.

title: The Secret Remedy
iast: śṛṇu devī! paraṁ guhyaṁ rahasyaṁ paramādbhutam | sarva-pāpa-praśamanaṁ sarva-duḥkha-nivāraṇam || prāyaścitteṣu sarveṣu tīvreṣv api vimocanam | sarva-cchidrāpa-haraṇaṁ sarvārti-vinivārakam || samayolaṅghane ghore japādeva vimocanam | bhoga-mokṣha-pradaṁ devī! sarva-siddhi-phalapradam ||
en: listen, goddess: the supreme secret, most wonderful — it pacifies all sins, removes all sorrows; releases even from intense atonement, removes every gap, uproots all affliction; in the breaking of the vows the remedy is the recitation alone — it grants enjoyment and liberation, goddess, the fruits of all accomplishments.
brief: These verses extol the capacity of sacred recitation to remove affliction and wrongdoing. Such benefits are claims of the tradition, not verifiable clinical effects.
logic: Entrust the problem to Bhairava while remaining ready to act responsibly in the world.
howto: When: For a deliberate period of prayer, rather than in a queue. Practice: Read the complete source-verified three-verse passage, without pressure to memorise all of it. If a brief line is chosen later, label it as an extract, not a mantra. Return: Address what can be addressed; seek practical help where needed.
how: Recite it at the beginning and end of any ritual — the hymn's own instruction (yāgārambhe ca yāgānte). Also daily (nitya), on occasion (naimitika), when you want something (kāmya), for yourself or for someone else. Counting effects per the hymn: one hundred recitations purify even great sinners; fifty, inadvertent sins; twenty-five, minor sins — and a single recitation (of this hymn or of the Aghora japa) removes wrongs done by body, speech or mind, whether through inattention or knowingly.
feel: the ease is the point — sadupāyaṁ, the remedy without strain.
sign: Everyday integration: Address what can be addressed; seek practical help where needed.

title: No Mantra Greater
iast: vidhihīne pramāde ca japtavyaṁ sarva-karmasu | nātaḥ parataro mantro nātaḥ paratarā stutiḥ || nātaḥ paratarā kācit samyak-pratyaṅgirā priye | iyaṁ samaya-vidyānāṁ rāja-rājeśvarī-śvari || paramāpyāyanaṁ devi bhairavasya prakīrtitam | prīṇanaṁ sarva-devānāṁ sarva-saubhāgya-vardhanam ||
en: when the rule is missing, when there is negligence — it should be recited in every action. no mantra is greater than this, no praise higher; no counter-formula better than this, o beloved — this queen of the knowledge of the precepts, o sovereign among isvaras! this, o goddess, is the supreme nourishment of bhairava's glorification — it satisfies all the gods and increases all good fortune.
brief: This close praises the efficacy of the mantra and the importance of reciting even when ritual procedure has been imperfect. Its superlative claims are internal to the hymn.
logic: Let the ritual finish without obsessively asking whether it was flawless.
howto: When: At the end of a deliberate ritual or an evening recitation. Practice: Recite the verified complete passage. If using the short phrase, remember it is a context-dependent assertion about this hymn, not a universal standalone invocation. Return: Put away the materials, and continue the evening.
how: Full practice in the tradition: dhyāna of Svacchanda (crystal-white upward face, yellow east, blue south, pomegranate-red north, moon-white west — the twelve-verse meditation), then this hymn, then the Gāyatrī — oṁ bahurupāya vidmahe, koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi, tanno 'ghoraḥ pracodayāt, three times — then the mūla mantra. In this book's simpler use: one round of these three verses at the close of any difficult day; the line to remember is 'no mantra greater than this'.
sign: Everyday integration: Put away the materials, and continue the evening.

title: Bahurūpa Gāyatrī
iast: oṁ bahurupāya vidmahe, koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi | tanno 'ghoraḥ pracodayāt
en:
we meditate on the manifold-formed,
on the one of a hundred thousand eyes —
may the aghora impel our thought.
brief: The Gāyatrī asks that Aghora direct or inspire understanding. The epithet koṭarākṣa needs a secure gloss from the textual tradition.
logic: The act is asking for guidance, not proving that a deity has intervened.
howto: When: When you deliberately want to begin a devotional recitation, not as an emergency shortcut. Practice: Recite it calmly once, or three times if following the supplied ritual sequence. Do not require breath holds or body sensations. Return: Return to the task with a more careful intention.
how: The recitation order per the viniyoga: dhyāna → hymn → this gāyatrī three times → mūla mantra. Three rounds, seed-voice. 'Pracodayāt' is the only request in the entire sequence — everything before it was arrangement.
sign: Everyday integration: Return to the task with a more careful intention.

title: Oṁ Namaḥ Śivāya
iast: oṁ namaḥ śivāya
en: Oṁ — I bow to Śiva.
brief: Oṃ; homage to Śiva. The mantra addresses and honours Śiva; Trika invites us also to discover that the one invoking is not ultimately separate from the invoked.
logic: Treat this as offering the next moment, not requesting a special sensation.
howto: When: At a threshold: standing up, leaving a room, or noticing that attention has become scattered. Practice: Say the entire mantra once, at a normal pace. A slight bow of the head is enough; no counting is required. Return: Do the next ordinary thing carefully.
sign: Everyday integration: Do the next ordinary thing carefully.
